name: Photos and PDFs sent to Happy are read and answered, behind a local privacy gate for text PDFs
description: Send a photo of a flyer, label or receipt, or a PDF packet, and Happy reads it and answers questions about it; today a message that is only an attachment is dropped without a reply. Before that is switched on, a check on the Mac refuses a PDF whose readable text looks like a bank statement or tax form and says why; scanned PDFs and photos cannot be checked and reach the cloud model unscreened.
example: Jordan sends a photo of a camp flyer and asks 'what do I need to bring?' and gets the answer in the same thread. Tony sends last month's bank e-statement PDF by mistake and gets a fixed line: this looks like a bank statement, so it was not sent to the cloud model.
how: Gate first (F084): an in-house plugin whose `before_agent_run` hook returns `outcome: "block"` on pattern hits in the extracted file text; it needs `plugins.entries.<id>.hooks.allowConversationAccess: true` and is proven with a seeded statement PDF before the switch goes on. Switch (F002): set `channels.imessage.includeAttachments: true`; Basic mode already carries media, with inbound caps of 10 MB for an image and 20 MB for audio. Images then pass natively to the reply model and attached PDFs arrive as extracted text blocks; the optional `pdf` tool (`group:media`) adds page selection through local PDFium, 10 MB and 20 pages by default. Set `tools.media.audio.enabled: false` until local transcription (F003) exists, and add one eval case: a PDF carrying hidden instructions must cause no tool call.
caveats: The gate reads only extracted text, so a scanned statement or a phone photo of one reaches the vision model unscreened; no local vision model exists to check photos.
Whether the extracted file text is inside the prompt the hook receives is untested, so the seeded-PDF test decides whether the gate works at all.

The same switch also lets voice memos and video in, and audio auto-detection tries a configured provider key before any local program, so audio understanding stays off until local transcription (F003) is in place and one live turn shows what a voice memo turns into.
Happy cannot watch video on this provider set, so an AGENTS.md line has it say so and ask for a photo or a few screenshots.
store:false covers less than it reads: OpenAI can keep abuse-monitoring logs, content included, for up to 30 days unless the organisation has Zero Data Retention, and family photos fall under that.
Whether medical bills and Explanation of Benefits statements are let through the gate is still to settle (from the folded 'explain this' entry).
A local classifier (OCL-14) could later replace the pattern match; it takes at most 512 tokens per input, so the gate would send the first lines of each page.
corrections: Catalog JSON 'needs' says view_image is already granted and sets agents.defaults.pdfModel to luna. The minimal profile contains only session_status and gateway (tool-policy.md:36), and pdfModel is an agents.defaults key that is unset by default (pdf.md:124). The Markdown already drops both.
unverified: Reading accuracy on blurry phone photos and scanned image-only PDFs was not measured; pages with under 200 characters of text are rendered to images for the vision model (pdf.md:93).
Whether PDF links, as opposed to attachments, should be readable is left open; the pdf tool rejects remote URLs when it runs sandboxed (pdf.md:68).
That the gateway process under the happy account already has Full Disk Access to the Messages attachments folder comes from the 9 Oct notes and was not re-checked.
Whether OpenClaw treats the per-person custom provider ids exactly like the stock OpenAI provider for image input was not tested live (the config repo does declare image input for both models).
That the extracted file text is inside the prompt field the hook receives; the doc only says the hook gets the current user input. Needs a test with a seeded PDF.
Which config key holds allowedMimes for iMessage attachments; the only documented allowedMimes keys sit under the Gateway HTTP API endpoints.
The exact point at which an inbound PDF falls back to page images; the 200-characters-per-page rule is documented for the pdf tool, not for channel attachments.
Photo gating is blocked, not just weak: no local vision model exists on this install, so only a caption keyword rule is possible.
safety: A photo or PDF is outside content read by the agent that holds a parent's memory. That agent cannot browse, and its texts and the scheduled jobs it can create are pinned to the family by the hook in G009 (F007 waits for that hook). The roadmap names one way out that is neither closed nor pinned: the hand-off to the research helper (F019), which can fetch any public address and is guarded only by a prompt rule and an eval case. So the eval case listed here (a PDF carrying hidden instructions must cause no tool call) has to count a hand-off to research as a tool call. The gate runs on the Mac before any cloud call, can only block, and blocks if it fails. It is a tripwire for text PDFs, not a guarantee.

name: Voice over iMessage, kept on the Mac mini: voice memos in, spoken replies out
description: A parent sends a voice memo instead of typing; the Mac mini transcribes it, echoes the text back and answers, and after a voice memo or on request the reply also arrives as an audio file made on the Mac mini (the built-in macOS voice first, a more natural voice later). Speech stays on the Mac only with the transcriber listed explicitly and the default-on Microsoft online voice switched off, and whether the audio file itself is withheld from the cloud chat model is still to be confirmed on a live turn.
example: Jordan sends a voice memo: 'what's on tomorrow?' Happy echoes the transcript, answers in text and attaches the same answer as audio. Or a parent sends `/tts latest` after a long answer.
how: In (F003): an explicit `tools.media.models` CLI entry for `whisper-cli` (audio capability, `{{AttachmentPath}}`) plus `echoTranscript`; needs Homebrew whisper.cpp, ffmpeg and a GGML model file, and OpenClaw converts to WAV itself. Out (VOX-04), step 1 with no install: the gateway `tts` block with provider `tts-local-cli` running the macOS `say` command, `tts.auto: "inbound"` per agent so a voice memo gets a spoken answer, and `/tts latest` on demand; set `tts.providers.microsoft.enabled: false` and keep speech off for the research and inbox agents. Later step: a natural voice by one of three documented routes (Speech Swift's loopback server behind the `openai` speech provider, the `speech` command through `tts-local-cli`, or a Piper voice through sherpa-onnx).
caveats: A parent can already dictate a message with the iPhone keyboard and send it as text, and the roadmap schedules voice memos with the kids' voice milestone, so for the two adults this is a convenience and not a new ability.

Local-only is not the default in either direction: audio auto-detection tries a configured provider key before any local program, and the keyless Microsoft online voice is enabled by default and can serve as a fallback, so both are pinned in config.

`/tts provider <id>` is open to any authorized sender and changes the provider for everyone, so having no cloud speech provider configured is the control, and the bundled `sag` skill (ElevenLabs, a cloud voice) stays off.
The reply is a plain audio file attachment (WAV, several megabytes for a few minutes), not a voice bubble; the voice-bubble option belongs to the Private API actions, which need SIP off.
Long replies are summarised by the cloud chat model before synthesis, or truncated; for kids' content later that step must be local or off.

The natural-voice routes add a third-party Homebrew package from a 0.0.x project, a loopback server with its own launchd job and a model download; none of `speech`, `speech-server` or `ffmpeg` is installed today.
Transcription speed and accuracy for Chinese or mixed-language speech, and whether ffmpeg decodes the iMessage voice-memo format cleanly, were not measured.
Talk mode (part of the iPhone app entry, OCL-01) has its own speech setting and does not pick up this voice automatically.
corrections: Markdown pairs a whisper-cpp install with audio.preferredModel: "cli:whisper". The matcher compares that value with cli: plus the entry's exact command string (dist/resolve-KJuMET3H.mjs:148), so for whisper-cpp it must be cli:whisper-cli, or cli: plus the full path used in the entry; cli:whisper only matches the Python whisper CLI.

The Homebrew formula is now named whisper.cpp (formerly whisper-cpp) and its page says GGML model files are not downloaded by default. The 9 Oct note about a model that downloads automatically describes the Python whisper CLI (media-understanding.md:168), not whisper-cli.

ffmpeg is a hard requirement the Markdown leaves out: upstream whisper-cli reads only 16-bit WAV (github.com/ggml-org/whisper.cpp README), OpenClaw shells out to ffmpeg for that conversion (dist/ffmpeg-exec-VIr-PIWC.mjs:25 prints the brew install hint), and the formula does not pull ffmpeg in.
unverified: The container format of iMessage voice memos, and whether ffmpeg decodes it cleanly, were not tested.
Transcription speed on the M5 Pro and accuracy for Chinese or mixed-language speech were not measured.
Whether the per-person custom provider ids count as OpenAI audio auth in auto-detection is undocumented; the explicit CLI entry sidesteps the question.

That only the transcript reaches the cloud model: the media docs say the original attachment is still passed to the model, and the model's listed inputs are text and image, so the audio file should be left out, but this was not checked on a live turn.
Kokoro or Piper voice quality and speed on this Mac.
Whether pointing `tts.providers.openai` at loopback has any side effect on the earlier decision not to add a catalog openai model provider (it is a different config block).
Whether scheduled announce deliveries (briefs) pass through Auto-TTS or only interactive replies do.
Which hosts the Speech Swift package contacts to download its models.

Whether a failed local synthesis actually falls through to the Microsoft online provider when only one provider block is written. The docs say other configured providers are fallbacks and that Microsoft is enabled by default; this was not tested.
That the documented say preset writes a valid WAV on macOS 27 without extra data-format flags was not run.
How Messages on iPhone presents a WAV attachment (inline player or plain file) was not tested.
The 1,500-character summarise-or-truncate threshold is documented (tts/commands.md:104) but its effect on long replies here was not tried.
safety: Speech-to-text runs on the Mac mini; the transcript goes to the cloud chat model like any typed message, and whether the audio file is withheld from it is an open check. Synthesis adds no way to send data out and is local only once cloud speech providers are disabled. A voice memo comes from an allowlisted parent and brings no outside content.

name: Family-only delivery: text the other parent or the parents' group, and ask-and-relay a yes or no, with the recipient pinned in code
description: Happy can send a text to the other parent or to the parents' group and to nobody else: a short note one parent asks it to pass on, a notice from another feature (for example the line that says the model is down), or a question whose yes or no it relays back, with one reminder before the ask expires. A check in code that fails closed refuses any recipient outside the family.
example: Tony texts: 'Ask Jordan if she can do Thursday pickup.' Jordan gets one line, answers 'yes', and Tony gets her answer back.
how:
Delivery (G009): the `message` tool on

-main with a `before_tool_call` plugin hook that blocks any target not in family.json5 and fails closed. The live config has both `tools.message.crossContext` switches off, which confines sends to the current conversation, so `allowWithinProvider` is turned back on (`allowAcrossProviders` stays off) and the hook is then the only recipient limit. Host jobs use `openclaw agent --deliver` or `openclaw message send`. Request relay (G010), an optional second step that need not hold up the first: a pending_requests table in the household store, a `before_dispatch` plugin that matches a bare yes or no from the asked parent to that parent's one open request, and a one-shot `--at` automation for the reminder and the expiry. The same hook also has to check the scheduling tool from the moment F007 grants it: that tool's add and update calls accept a delivery target, a webhook address and separate completion and failure destinations, so the hook refuses webhook delivery and any job target other than the asking parent.
caveats: A parent can always text the other parent directly or ask in the parents' group chat (F006), so passing a note or relaying a question through Happy is a small convenience; the relay adds only tracking, one reminder and an expiry. What the first step really adds is one family-only limit, enforced in code, that Happy's own notices and the later features that must reach both parents all go through.
Only the before_tool_call check fails closed; a message_sending hook can be added as a second check but is logged and skipped when its handler throws or times out, so it must not be relied on.
Re-opening the same-provider crossContext switch makes the hook the only recipient limit, and the hook and its family-only test case do not exist yet.
In iMessage Basic mode there is no tap-to-answer, so the reply to a relayed request is a typed yes or no.
For anyone outside the family (a plumber, a coach, carpool parents) Happy returns paste-ready wording and the parent sends it from their own phone.
corrections: Markdown adds message_sending 'as a second gate'. That hook can cancel a send, but when its handler throws or times out it is logged and skipped (hooks/reference.md:94), so it fails open; only the before_tool_call check is fail-closed.

The 9 Oct 'needs' implies that enabling the tool plus the hook is enough. The live config turns both crossContext switches off, and tool-permissions.md:39 says that confines sends to the current conversation, so the same-provider switch must be re-opened and the hook then becomes the only recipient limit.
unverified: The exact parameter that carries the recipient in a message tool call, which the hook must match, was not read from source.
openclaw message send takes no agent flag and runs as the configured System Agent (cli/message.md:35-50); whether that suits per-person jobs was not tested.
The hook plugin and its family-only test case do not exist yet, so blocking an unknown recipient is unproven on this install.
How plugin code sends the relayed answer on to the other parent: no plugin-side outbound send call was found in the docs read, so the relay step may have to send through this entry's first step.
Group-chat use assumes iMessage groups, which are switched off today.
Judgement, not sourced: the parents can already text each other, so the relay's gain is only tracking, one reminder and an expiry.
safety:
This is the house rule that outbound messages go only to the family, enforced by code that fails closed and not by a prompt. It gives

-main, which holds private data and reads outside content (attachments, search and research results, calendar text), a way out limited to the two parents and their group chat. Inside that limit the hook checks who receives a text, not what the text says: an injected instruction could still make one parent's agent text that parent's private notes to the other parent. That stays in the family but crosses the roadmap's rule of one data domain per person, and the roadmap's own recipient test (written for the email send tool) counts another family member as a wrong recipient, so accepting it is part of the decision listed under the prerequisites. The relay step adds no new recipient and no new data source.

demand.title: Tool and agent permissions
demand.supports: OpenClaw documents that an agent holding the message tool can send to other conversations by default; this entry switches that on for the same channel only and pins it to the family with a hook that blocks when it fails, the mechanism the roadmap uses to pin email to its owner.

depends_on: family.json5 registry (the list of allowed recipients)

Decision: the roadmap's Replies rule keeps both crossContext switches off (no sends into other conversations, scheduled jobs deliver only to their owner); this entry relaxes it to sends on the same channel, pinned to the family by the hook. Saying yes also accepts that one parent's agent can put what it holds in front of the other parent, which the roadmap's rule of one data domain per person and its email recipient test (another family member counts as a wrong recipient) would not allow

name: Built-in chat commands for parents (/stop, /new, /status, /usage, /tools)
description: A handful of typed commands that already work in the iMessage thread: stop an answer that is going wrong, start a clean conversation, see what Happy can do right now, and check health and cost, all handled before any model call. One more does use the model: /btw asks a side question that is not remembered (its page does not list iMessage, so treat it as untested here).
example: Jordan texts '/stop' when a long answer is heading the wrong way, then '/new'. Tony texts '/status' when Happy seems slow.
how: Text commands are core and work on iMessage: command-only messages from allowlisted senders are handled before the queue and the model. /stop aborts the active run in that chat; /new archives the session and starts fresh; /tools lists the agent's effective tools; /status shows runtime, uptime and plugin health; /usage tokens|full|cost toggles a per-reply footer or prints a cost summary. /btw answers from the current session with a separate one-shot model query and writes nothing to history. Put the five everyday ones in templates/person/AGENTS.md and a one-screen cheat sheet. The config-writing commands stay off as today, and Tony should decide whether /restart and /update, which one switch (commands.restart, on by default) opens to owners, stay available from chat.
depends_on: Decision: whether /restart and /update stay available from chat (one switch, commands.restart, on by default, opens both to owners)
A one-screen cheat sheet for both parents, and the five commands listed in templates/person/AGENTS.md
caveats: /stop ends one run in one chat; it does not pause scheduled jobs, so it complements the G005 kill phrase rather than replacing it.
The /btw page names WhatsApp, Telegram and Discord for channel use and does not mention iMessage.
/btw is a separate one-shot model call on the session's model; it is not free and not model-less.
/usage figures are local estimates, not the provider's bill.
In a plain iMessage bubble the /status and /tools output may be long.

/loop is left off the cheat sheet. It is an owner-only command that has the agent create a repeating job through the scheduling tool, so it does nothing until F007 grants that tool, and a job made this way sits outside the G003 jobs registry. Its prerequisites and house rule are recorded with the multi-day project entry (AUT-01); a loop on a parent's agent sees only search snippets, so watching a page or a feed belongs to the model-free watchers (F018).
safety:
No new capability for the five everyday commands: they are read from the sender's own message, authorised by the sender allowlist and the owner list, and handled before the model runs. /btw is a model turn on

-main under its normal tool policy, and

-main cannot browse.

name: Timed reminders over iMessage (one-shot and recurring)
description: "Remind me at 4:30 to pick up the kids" or "every Sunday 7 pm: bins out" becomes a scheduled text to the asker, and reminders can be listed and cancelled.
example: Tony texts: 'Remind me at 4:30 to pick up the kids.' At 4:30 he gets a text from Happy: 'Pick up the kids.' Later he texts 'what reminders do I have?' and then 'cancel the bins one'.
how:
automations tool (cron alias) allowed on

-main, but only once the G009 before_tool_call hook also checks this tool's add and update calls; --at one-shots auto-delete; recurring --cron with --tz; every reminder job carries an empty tool list (--tools "" on the command line, the toolsAllow field when the agent creates the job); cron.triggers.enabled: false; only senders in commands.ownerAllowFrom may use it.
caveats: For a plain personal timer, Siri and the iPhone Reminders app already do the job, including reminders tied to a place or to messaging a chosen person. Happy's version earns its place for reminders that come out of something Happy just read or answered, and because the same scheduler carries the briefs, watchers and other timed jobs.

Once the Reminders bridge (F030) exists, 'remind me' can mean two things: a text from Happy at a set time (this entry) or an item on an Apple Reminders list. OpenClaw's bundled Reminders skill tells the agent to ask which is meant when it is unclear; the bridge here is an in-house plugin, so the same rule goes into AGENTS.md.

Once a parent is a command owner and their agent holds the scheduling tool, that agent can list, inspect, update, run or remove any job on the gateway, whoever created it (managing-jobs.md:79). Tony's agent could then read or change Jordan's reminders and the generated briefs, watchers and digests, and hers could do the same to his once she is an owner. Decide whether to accept that between two adults or to have the family-only hook refuse changes to jobs another agent runs. The job list does report which agent runs each job (effectiveAgentId, managing-jobs.md:165), but a hook that uses it was not tried.

If that decision goes against granting the tool, a dated item on a Reminders list (F030) is the route that needs no scheduling tool: OpenClaw's bundled Reminders skill describes to-dos with due dates that sync to the phone. F030 as specified sets no due dates, and that the alert reaches the asker's phone from a shared list would need a test.
corrections: Catalog JSON 'needs' lists --delete-after-run. One-shot --at jobs already delete themselves after confirmed delivery (how-it-works.md:19). The Markdown already says so.
unverified: Creating a reminder from an iMessage owner turn has not been tried live on this install; managing-jobs.md:81 describes chat creation for Control UI administrators, and the owner-only /loop command is the documented chat shortcut for recurring jobs.
The comparison with Siri and Apple Reminders for one-off personal timers was not sourced.
safety:
This is a control-plane tool: OpenClaw's guidance is to deny it by default to any agent that handles outside content (tool-permissions.md:21), and

-main reads search results, attachments and relayed research text. The tool lets the agent name where a job's output goes: another chat target, or a web address (delivery mode webhook, plus separate completion and failure destinations). On the agent that holds a parent's memory that would be a way to send data out, so the tool is granted only after the family-only hook (G009) refuses webhook delivery and any target other than the asking parent, and with cron.triggers.enabled: false so that no script payload or trigger script can be created. A job an agent creates keeps the tools of the turn that made it unless its tool list is set (payloads.md:60), so the hook should also require an empty tool list on a reminder job; its timed run can then only produce text. A command owner's agent can also list, change, run or remove every job on the gateway, not only its owner's (managing-jobs.md:79), so an injected instruction could read, rewrite or switch off another person's reminder or a generated job. The hook as specified checks only add and update calls for where the output goes; refusing update, run and remove on jobs the asking parent's agent did not create would close this, and whether a job list can be trimmed the same way is unchecked.

name: Family calendar, read-only: 'what's on Saturday?' and 'is anyone free Friday at 1?'
description: "What's on Saturday?" or "is anyone free Friday at 1?" is answered from the family Google Calendar, read-only; it also feeds the daily briefs.
example: Jordan texts: 'What's on Saturday?' and gets the day's events from the family calendar. Tony asks 'is anyone free Friday at 1?' and gets what the family calendar shows for that hour; nothing on the calendar is changed.
how: Host-side stdio MCP server per person. Sign-in: `gog auth add <account> --services calendar --readonly`, so the grant covers Calendar only (the default, `--services user`, authorizes gog's whole default set of user services). Server: `gog --account <account> mcp --allow-tool calendar_events`, because by default the server registers every read tool, mail and Drive search included. 'Is anyone free?' is answered by listing that hour's events with the same tool. gog's free/busy and conflicts exist only as command-line commands; a wrapper for them belongs to the conflict watch (MKT-06) and is not part of this entry. Allow bundle-mcp in the sandbox gate; publish the OAuth app.
caveats: Public feeds (the school district calendar, library and recreation events, team schedules) show up in Happy's calendar answers only after the family Google Calendar is subscribed to each feed link, which Google allows from a computer browser only; a search of the installed OpenClaw docs and skills found no .ics handling of its own. Google gives no refresh interval and TeamSnap says changes can take up to 24 hours to appear, so change alerts are a separate job (the model-free watchers, F018).

'Is anyone free?' is answered only from events the asking parent's sign-in can see: the family calendar, and that parent's own calendars unless the tool can be pinned to one calendar. The other parent's work or personal calendar is not read, so 'free' means 'nothing on the family calendar'. gog's server offers one calendar tool, the events list, and no free/busy tool; reading each parent's own calendar as busy-only is the wider grant described under the conflict watch (MKT-06).
corrections: The 9 Oct wording has Tony hand-write the calendar MCP server. gogcli.sh/mcp.html documents a built-in stdio server (gog --account <account> mcp) with a read-only calendar_events tool and an --allow-tool filter, so listing events needs no custom code. Freebusy and conflicts exist only as CLI commands (gogcli.sh/commands) and still need a wrapper.

Catalog JSON 'needs' expects a calendar.readonly scope from --services calendar. The documented switch is --readonly on gog auth add; Google's scope list does include calendar.readonly (developers.google.com/workspace/calendar/api/auth). The Markdown asked to verify the flag; gog's command page confirms it.
unverified: gog is not installed on this Mac, so its flags were read from gogcli.sh and not from the binary; the bundled skill names the brew formula gogcli while the site shows a tap-qualified name.
Whether gog's calendar_events MCP tool can be pinned to a single calendar id was not confirmed.
Google or iCloud is still Tony's open decision; the iCloud route needs the OpenClaw macOS app paired as a node, which is not installed.
That events from a URL-subscribed calendar are returned through the Google Calendar API, and so through gog, was not confirmed.
Whether this family's district, club and library actually publish feed links was not checked.

That `--services calendar` with `--readonly` yields a calendar-only read grant, and that `--allow-tool calendar_events` leaves no other tool registered, were read from gogcli.sh and not run; `gog mcp --list-tools` prints the registered set and is the check to run once gog is installed. Which services gog's default `user` set contains is not listed on the page opened.

Once the mail agent (G015) signs the same Google account in for Gmail, the calendar-only grant holds only if the two sign-ins are stored apart. gog's auth page lists a --home switch (its own config and token folder) and a --client switch (a named token bucket), but does not say whether a second sign-in for the same account replaces or widens the first.
safety: Read-only and calendar-only by construction: each account is added for the Calendar service alone with gog's --readonly switch, which asks Google for read-only access and blocks changes at runtime, and the server is narrowed to the events-listing tool. Without those two limits the sign-in would cover gog's default set of Google services rather than Calendar alone, and the server would register every read tool it has, mail and Drive search among them, on the agent that holds a parent's memory, which the roadmap keeps apart from mail. Event titles and descriptions can be written by people outside the family (an invitation, a subscribed public feed), and OpenClaw says its sender controls do not sanitize tool results (hardened-baseline.md:42), so calendar text is outside content read by that agent. It cannot browse and its texts are pinned to the family (G009); the way out that the roadmap itself names as still open is the hand-off to the research helper (F019).

name: Research helper: reads public web pages and answers with the link and the time fetched; it holds no family data and cannot reach the home network
description: Happy can read public web pages that load without JavaScript or a login: a memory-less research helper fetches the page and the parent's own agent relays the answer with its link and the time it was fetched. Slow lookups get an 'on it', one message when done and a working 'cancel that', and nothing the helper fetches can reach the home network.
example: Jordan texts: 'What time does the town pool open on Saturday? Check their site.' Happy replies 'on it', then sends the hours with the link and when the page was fetched.
how:
Agent (F019): a new `research` agent, memory search off, tools `web_search` and `web_fetch`, sandboxed; each

-main gains `sessions_spawn` and `subagents.allowAgents: ["research"]`; its rules live in AGENTS.md only. Guardrails (WEB-01): leave both `dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork` keys unset, keep `tools.web.fetch.headers` empty, install no fetch-provider plugin, set `browser.evaluateEnabled: false`, keep `browser.enabled: false` until F020, and add two eval cases (a LAN address, a public URL that redirects to one) to the M3 exit test. Answer rules (F022): quote `fetchedAt`, use `published` when present, flag pages undated or older than 30 days, allow 'could not verify'; a fact check returns true, false, mixed or unclear with two or three dated sources. Etiquette (G014): `runTimeoutSeconds` on the spawn, the automatic completion announce, `subagents` `action: "cancel"`, and concurrency caps.
caveats: The plain fetch runs no JavaScript and cannot log in, so such pages wait for the research browser (F020) or stay unread.

web_fetch blocks private hosts and re-checks redirects, but the browser's own check is weaker (the docs say its request interception is not a network firewall), which matters once F020 switches the browser on.

Leave the private-network keys truly unset: an explicitly written `browser.ssrfPolicy.dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork: false` turns hostname navigation into an allowlist and would stop a later research browser from loading hostnames.

The SSRF policy covers the `web_fetch` and browser tools only, so host-side helpers that take a URL (the summarize wrapper, the print plugin's download, watcher scripts) need their own scheme, host and resolved-address checks.

A hostname block list is not an exfiltration control and is not worth curating: what counts is the private-network block, no headers, no fallback provider, and no private data in the agent that browses.

Once research has web_fetch, the roadmap's egress proxy cannot double as an exfiltration allowlist; it can deny private ranges and named hosts and nothing more (an inference from the routing description).
A sandboxed requester cannot spawn an unsandboxed target, so research has to stay sandboxed, and sub-agents keep only AGENTS.md, so every citation and no-login rule must be in that one file.
An official-sites-only mode for admin questions would need a before_tool_call hook and is not planned.

The home-network block rests on the fetch tool resolving and pinning the address itself. If web_fetch is ever routed through the roadmap's egress proxy with `tools.web.fetch.useTrustedEnvProxy: true`, OpenClaw keeps only the hostname check and leaves address resolution to the proxy, so that switch stays off unless the proxy denies private ranges after it resolves the name. With the switch off, web_fetch connects directly even when proxy variables are set (cli/doctor/checks.md:51), so the roadmap's deny-by-default firewall would have to allow that traffic (an inference from the roadmap's firewall line); which of the two it will be is settled when the proxy goes in.
corrections: The 9 Oct verifier notes advised turning the sandbox off for research; the installed docs say a sandboxed requester cannot spawn an unsandboxed target, so the catalog's final wording (keep mode all) is the only workable one.
A verifier note asked for research rules in AGENTS.md and SOUL.md; the installed docs say sub-agents keep only AGENTS.md, so every citation and no-login rule must be in that one file.
unverified: That a cross-agent handoff returns its result with agent-to-agent messaging off: the roadmap lists this as untested on 2026.9.7 and the CLI was not run here.

The handoff privacy rule (ages yes, names and school no) is a prompt rule; nothing mechanical enforces what

-main writes into the task text.
The roadmap's plan to drop LAN access inside the Colima VM would not cover a browser that runs on the host; this follows from where the process runs and was not tested.
Which hosts belong on the blocklist is a judgment call, not something the docs prescribe.
The explicit-false behaviour of the browser policy was read in the installed source only; the docs do not describe it and it was not exercised.
Nothing in the installed stack enforces citations; this is a prompt rule the model can ignore, and Tony's promptfoo evals are the only check.
The 30-day staleness threshold and the three-links-per-text cap are house choices with no source.
Nothing on the current stack runs longer than about 20 seconds, so the 'on it' and 'cancel that' convention is untried until this hand-off exists.
The acknowledgement wording and the 'about three minutes' estimate are prompt conventions; the model can skip them.
safety: The research agent reads untrusted pages but holds no memory, no accounts and no family data, and the guardrails take the home network out of its reach. That keeps private data away from the agent that browses; it does not close every path. The guardrails do not stop an injected page making the helper request some public URL, and the roadmap names the hand-off as the one remaining leak path: the parent's agent holds memory, reads search results, attachments and the helper's relayed answer, and writes the task text that goes to a helper able to fetch any public address. OpenClaw's guidance is to deny sessions_spawn by default to an agent that handles outside content (tool-permissions.md:21), so this grant is deliberate and narrow: the allowlist names only research, the rule about what may go into the task text is a prompt rule, and the roadmap's exit test includes an injected result that asks the parent's agent to pass memory to research. The relayed answer is treated as untrusted.

name: Shared Apple Reminders lists bridge (read, add, tick off)
description: Happy can read, add to and tick off items on the Reminders lists the family already shares, so changes show up on both parents' iPhones. That an item added from the Mac's command line reaches a list shared from a parent's account has not been tested; it is the first thing to prove.
example: After Happy answers 'what do I need for pancakes for six?', Jordan texts 'add the flour, eggs and buttermilk to the grocery list'. The three items appear on the shared list on both parents' phones. Later Tony texts 'what's still on the grocery list?' and gets the open items.
how: In-house host-side tool plugin wrapping remindctl (list/add/complete, named lists only, no delete); happy's Apple Account joins the shared lists; Reminders permission granted in the gateway's own process context.
caveats: A shared Apple Note as a second filing target is not part of this build. The memo command-line tool edits notes only through an interactive editor, and an unattended AppleScript append to a shared iCloud note has no opened source and no test. Treat it as a later experiment once the Reminders bridge works.

For a single item spoken to the phone, Siri already creates reminders with nothing to build (Apple's Reminders page documents asking Siri). The bridge earns its place when the items come out of something Happy read or planned (a recipe link, the meal plan, a flyer) and when a job needs to read a list.
unverified: No opened source confirms that remindctl can add to or complete items on a shared iCloud list owned by another family member; its README only says reminders sync through the normal iCloud path.
Which binary macOS records the Reminders permission against when the launchd gateway spawns remindctl is not documented in any opened source; it needs one test on happy's logged-in desktop.
The Notes half (appending to a shared folder with osascript) has no first-party Apple scripting reference opened in this run; the memo CLI page only confirms it relies on AppleScript and an editor.
safety: The tool offers only list, add and complete on named lists and has no delete. An item added to a shared list appears on the devices of everyone the list is shared with, so the lists Happy may write to should be shared only inside the family; otherwise an add would put text in front of someone outside it. Any participant can also type items, so list text read back by a parent's agent is outside content if a list is ever shared more widely.

name: Household store for dated schedules and single facts (in-house tool plugin)
description: A small household database that both parents' agents and the timed jobs read and update: dated schedules (filter every 90 days, last oil change) and single facts a job needs. It is the shared back end of the upkeep rows in the renewals look-ahead (F063) and of the other dated features; handbook-style knowledge lives in the vault (F043) and each parent's own notes in memory (F041).
example: Tony texts: 'did the furnace filter today'. Six weeks later Jordan asks 'when is the furnace filter due?' and gets the same date Tony's agent would give.
how: In-house defineToolPlugin over node:sqlite with schedule_get/upsert/mark_done and fact_get/set; allowlisted on both mains and in tools.sandbox.tools; secret check inside execute or via definePluginEntry.
caveats: The first version has only the schedule and fact tools. Features that keep their own rows here (the sick-day log in CRT-10, open requests in G009's relay step) add their own table and tool when they are built.
corrections: The 9 Oct verifier note says the secret-rejecting before_tool_call hook can live in the same plugin as the defineToolPlugin store. docs/plugins/tool-plugins.md:11 says defineToolPlugin adds tools only, and :233 points to definePluginEntry when tools are combined with hooks.

The catalog chooses defineToolPlugin for the store but still names its tools home-store__schedule_* in the automations. docs/tools/multi-agent-sandbox-tools.md:242 gives that server__tool form to MCP servers only; a plugin's tools carry the names it declares, so job tool lists must use those.
unverified: node:sqlite is labelled release candidate on nodejs.org; no long-run test of it inside the gateway process was done.
safety: Both parents' agents and the timed jobs read and write the same rows, so anything stored here is shared between the two adults by design; something meant for one parent belongs in that parent's own memory (F041). The plugin refuses values that look like secrets. Like a memory note, a stored fact is read back later by the other parent's agent and by jobs, so it is a place where an injected instruction could persist: facts should stay short and typed (a date, an interval, a short label), not free text lifted from a page or a document.

name: Durable per-person memory: 'remember this' is saved to that parent's own notes and found again, by keyword first and by meaning as a later step
description: A parent texts 'remember that...' and their own agent writes the fact to its notes and finds it again in later chats; where those notes live is an open decision that settles whether a saved note survives the next deploy and whether it is in view at the start of a chat or found only when Happy searches. Notes are found by their words at first; a later, optional step adds search by meaning for text notes, with the indexing done on the Mac mini.
example: Jordan texts: 'Remember that piano moved to Thursdays at 4.' A week later she asks 'which day is piano?' and gets Thursday at 4. After the later step, 'what was the kid's nut thing again?' finds the note that says 'tree-nut allergy', although none of the words match.
how: Notes (F041): allow write and edit on each parent's agent, with a read-write workspace and apply_patch denied by name; an in-house before_tool_call hook limits write paths, by default to memory/*.md (MEMORY.md and USER.md stay with the F042 generator unless a live test shows a chat write does not stop them loading); memory_search and memory_get with keyword-only search set explicitly (`memory.search.provider: "none"`; unset, the documented default is OpenAI embeddings); the bundled session-memory hook. Later step (F046): install the official llama.cpp provider plugin, run its embedding-only setup, set the provider to `local` with `fallback: "none"` and re-index; the same search also covers the family handbook (F043). Further option: Active Memory, which adds a blocking model call to each reply it runs on.
caveats: Where chat-saved notes live is undecided: as read in the installed docs and code and not tried on a live turn, a chat write to MEMORY.md or USER.md from a sender who is not the command owner (today every turn of Jordan's), after web content in the same turn, or after the family-facts generator (F042) has re-rendered the file marks the whole file untrusted, and an untrusted file no longer loads at the start of a chat, the generated family facts in it included.

Keeping saved notes in memory/*.md avoids that at a cost: only today's and yesterday's dated notes load at a fresh start and older ones are found only when the agent searches, so until the choice is made and tested for both parents a saved note is not guaranteed to come back.

MEMORY.md is loaded at the start of a parent's one-to-one chat but not in scheduled jobs, group chats or hand-offs to a helper, so a brief or a reminder does not know a saved note unless its job is given memory search.

Refusing a memory write in a turn that carried web or research results is not something the platform does for a file write: no taint flag that a hook can read was found, so the in-house hook has to track web tool calls itself, and this is untested.
Notes belong to one parent; something both parents should get the same answer to belongs in the household store (F031) or the family handbook (F043).
Until the later step is done a saved note is found by its words and not by its meaning, and whether keyword search finds a note saved in Chinese on the default index setting has not been tested.

Search by meaning covers text only, because on this version photo and audio indexing works only with Google's cloud embedding model, and how much it would improve on keyword search for a few hundred family notes is a judgement, not a measured figure.
If the embedding server on the Mac mini fails, search drops back to keyword matching without telling the parent; the reason shows only in a debug field.
corrections: The catalog relies on `sessions_search` with visibility `agent` to find pre-reset conversations. docs/gateway/config-tools/sessions-and-subagents.md:58 says a sandboxed session stays limited to sessions it spawned while agents.defaults.sandbox.sessionToolsVisibility is 'spawned' (the default); the mains run with sandbox mode all, so that key must change as well. docs/tools/multi-agent-sandbox-tools.md:372 adds that tools.sessions.visibility is gateway-wide, not per agent.

The catalog ties this to M2 (local models). docs/plugins/llama-cpp.md:123 documents an embedding-only setup that adds no chat model, so the text leg does not depend on M2 and can be done on the installed stack.

The 9 Oct reason for dropping photo search is that no local multimodal embedder exists. Google's EmbeddingGemma page now describes EmbeddingGemma 2 as multimodal and local; the actual block is that OpenClaw 2026.9.7 only indexes images with gemini-embedding-2 (docs/reference/memory-config.md:495).
unverified: Whether visibility 'self' already reaches the same chat's pre-reset history (the docs define self as the current session key) was not tested.

No taint flag that a plugin hook can read was found in the hook docs opened, although OpenClaw's memory design does mark a turn as tainted after web content (memory-architecture.md:117); so 'refuse writes after web results' means the hook tracking web tool calls itself. Untested.

How a direct agent write to a memory file is classified was read in the installed code, not seen on a live turn: the write is recorded as agent-written only in a command owner's turn with no web content, and only if the file has not changed since its last recorded write; otherwise the whole file is recorded as untrusted (dist/agent-tools-D5UK6LHM.mjs:496, dist/memory-artifact-provenance-D8JQrziA.mjs:76). MEMORY.md and USER.md load at the start of a chat only while their record counts as eligible (memory-architecture.md:215). Check on a live turn for each parent.
Whether a note saved in one of Jordan's turns (she is not the command owner) comes back from memory_search like any other note, or is shown to the model with an untrusted label, was not tested.
Whether the F042 generator keeps lines Happy saved by chat was not checked; the generator was not opened.

Whether keyword search finds a note saved in Chinese on the default index setting was not tested: the engine page lists Chinese support through trigram tokenization (memory-builtin.md:23), the config reference gives `unicode61` as the default tokenizer with `trigram` as the alternative (reference/memory-config.md:625), and the search guide's fix for Chinese text that is not found is a forced re-index (memory-search.md:226). F042's own example has Jordan writing to Happy in Chinese, so the live test should include one such note.

How an untrusted label is cleared once it is set was not found: in the code read, the label recorded for a file is returned without comparing it with the file's current contents (dist/memory-path-provenance-BiFQlpIk.mjs:49), so a re-render by the generator may not bring a file back into the start of a chat.
Whether the managed llama.cpp server in 2026.9.7 can load EmbeddingGemma 2 was not checked.
The gain over keyword search for a few hundred family notes is a judgement, not a sourced figure.
Whether search by meaning finds a note saved in Chinese from a question asked in English, or the reverse, was not tested; it depends on the embedding model chosen.
safety: Notes stay in each parent's own agent; shared agents such as research hold none. A fail-closed before_tool_call hook limits writes to the memory files, and apply_patch is denied by name. A saved note is where an injected instruction could persist; the weekly review (G006) shows what was saved. The later step embeds on the Mac mini with no cloud fallback and adds no tool or send path.

name: Family facts, standing preferences and reply language rendered into each parent's agent from family.json5
description: Both parents' agents start every one-to-one chat already knowing the kids' school, routines and activities and each adult's standing preferences, including the language to reply in. On request Happy also turns a school note into a short Chinese text a parent can forward to a grandparent.
example: Jordan writes to Happy in Chinese and is answered in Chinese; Tony texts 'put this school note in Chinese for grandma' and gets three short lines to forward.
how: One generator, one file. From family.json5 the generator renders each adult's directives into USER.md (4,000-character cap), the per-person reply-language line among them (G011), and the kid and routine facts into MEMORY.md with trigger comments (F042); nothing is rendered into shared agents. A scheduled job does not infer a reply language from the chat and does not load MEMORY.md, so the language, and any family fact a job needs, is written into the job message or AGENTS.md. The two rendered files stay generator-only: what a parent asks Happy to remember in chat is saved elsewhere (F041). The grandparent version is a prompt-only request on the parent's own agent: no new tool and no send path, and the parent forwards the text.
caveats: USER.md has a 4,000-character cap that all standing preferences share, so the list has to stay short.

Rendered facts change only when the family file is edited and redeployed, and a chat edit to a generated file is expected to be lost on the next deploy; things a parent says in chat go through the memory write path (F041).

The kid and routine facts sit in MEMORY.md, which loads at the start of a parent's one-to-one chat only: scheduled jobs, the group chat and hand-offs to a helper do not get it (user-model.md:376), so a brief that needs a routine carries it in AGENTS.md or in its job message.

Happy should not write to the two rendered files from chat. OpenClaw records where each memory file's last write came from, and a write in a turn from a sender who is not the command owner (Jordan today), a write after web content, or a second chat write after the generator has re-rendered the file marks the whole file untrusted, after which it is no longer loaded at the start of a chat (memory-architecture.md:112 and :217; dist/agent-tools-D5UK6LHM.mjs:496; dist/memory-artifact-provenance-D8JQrziA.mjs:76). Read, not tried on a live turn; the write hook in F041 is where this is enforced.

On supported iPhones Messages can already translate a conversation automatically and on device, so plain back-and-forth with a grandparent may need nothing from Happy; whether that covers Chinese on this family's phones is not confirmed.
Happy's distinct part on the language side is the shortened Chinese version of a school note, and its translation quality for school notices was not evaluated.

A per-language voice switch is documented only for the bundled Microsoft speech provider, which is an online service, so it does not help the offline say path, and whether the default say voice pronounces Chinese was not tested.
The generator script and the family registry were not opened in this review.
corrections: A 9 Oct verifier note says there is no per-language voice switch. tts/output.md:56 documents one for the bundled Microsoft provider, which is an online service; it does not help the offline say path.
unverified: The generator script and the family registry live in happy-config and were not opened in this run.
That a chat edit to a generated file is lost on the next deploy is a property of Tony's generator, not something an opened source states.
Translation quality into Chinese by gpt-6-sol for school notices was not evaluated.
Which iPhone models and languages Apple's Live Translation covers for this family was not confirmed; the Apple page defers to an availability list.
Whether the macOS say default voice pronounces Chinese text was not tested.

Whether a scheduled run loads USER.md was not tried on a live job: the installed code lists it among the files a scheduled run gets and leaves MEMORY.md out (dist/workspace-DmDIneFk.mjs:742), while the scheduler guide only says a job does not infer a reply language (cron-jobs/delivery.md:140).

No tool and no send path are added; a translated note leaves the family only when a parent forwards it.

name: Household knowledge vault: shared family handbook, including the home systems and service-provider registry
description: One shared family handbook that both parents' agents can search: people, home systems, providers, policy and warranty summaries, sitter notes. Dates that need a reminder live in the renewals table (F063), not here. A photo of an appliance's data plate, sent once, fills in the home-systems page, so a later 'what filter does the furnace take?' or 'who fixed the boiler?' gets the stored answer.
example: Tony sends a photo of the furnace data plate and texts 'save this'. A month later Jordan asks: 'What filter does the furnace take?'
how: Step 1 (F043): a shared Markdown folder added to each main's `memory.search.extraPaths`. Step 2: enable the bundled memory-wiki plugin with `vault.scope` global and its own vault directory; `wiki_search`, `wiki_get`, `wiki_apply` and `wiki_lint` on the two mains only. Registry (F034): with inbound attachments on, the vision model reads the data plate and the agent saves a wiki synthesis page with `wiki_apply`, or a fact in the household store; manuals given as a link go through the research agent. With only step 1 in place, the operator types the plate details into the folder by hand.
caveats: The two installed pages disagree on whether enabling memory-wiki needs a gateway restart.
That memory_search in a sandboxed main can read a shared folder outside its workspace was not tested.
Saving a data plate as a wiki page needs step 2; with only the shared folder the operator types the details in by hand.
Data-plate photos go to the cloud vision model, which is the attachments decision recorded under F002, and image input on the family's custom provider ids was not re-checked.
The vault is shared by design, so both parents' agents search and edit the same pages.

Other entries file into it: the renewals look-ahead keeps a policy's one-line summary page here, and a pet's vet contact and food reorder link would sit in the provider registry, with nothing ordered.
unverified: The two installed pages disagree on whether enabling memory-wiki needs a gateway restart (docs/plugins/memory-wiki.md:26 says it applies to a running gateway, docs/cli/wiki.md:15 shows a restart).

That memory_search in a sandboxed main can read a shared folder outside its workspace was not tested. The installed code labels files indexed from outside an agent's workspace as untrusted origin (dist/memory-path-provenance-BiFQlpIk.mjs:32); whether that changes how handbook pages come back from search was not tested either.
That gpt-6-sol accepts images on Tony's custom provider ids was not checked in this run.
The memory-wiki route needs that bundled plugin enabled (F043 step 2); with only the shared Markdown folder, the operator types the plate details in by hand.
safety: Vault pages are private family data and stay on the two parents' own agents, which have no browse tool; the research agent that reads manuals holds none of it. A data-plate photo is untrusted content read by an agent with memory, but that agent can reply only to its owner or, once family delivery exists, the family.

name: Teach Happy a routine (operator-reviewed skills), with a parent-run practice quiz as the first skill
description: A parent describes once how the family does something (party plan, ski-trip packing, school-form explainer); Tony turns it into a named skill, and after the next deploy Happy can load it when a later request fits the skill's one-line description. The first skill is a practice quiz that a parent runs from a study-guide photo, a pasted spelling list or a request for math facts: ten questions, one at a time, hint first, a running score and the answer key at the end.
example: 'Happy, learn our ski-trip packing routine: ask how many nights and who is coming, then list by person, and always include the kids' helmets.' Or Jordan sends a photo of the science study guide and texts: 'quiz us on this, 10 questions, one at a time.'
how:
Pipeline (AUT-06): Happy answers with the drafted procedure as plain text; Tony turns it into `skills//SKILL.md` in happy-config, reviews it, and happy-deploy copies it into that agent's workspace `skills/` folder. The model loads a skill by reading its SKILL.md, so `

-main` needs `read` in `tools.alsoAllow` and the sandbox tool allowlist; `skill_workshop` stays denied on every family agent. A routine of a few lines can live in AGENTS.md instead. Quiz (MKT-02): one such skill fixes the format (one question per message, one hint before revealing, a running score, the answer key at the end, no web lookups); a photo needs attachment intake (F002) and is read by the reply model's own vision; an optional one-shot reminder offers a re-quiz the night before.
depends_on: a skills step in happy-deploy and gen-family
automatic self-learning switched off in config (`skills.workshop.autonomous.mode: "off"`)
decision: who may request a new skill

`read` allowed on

-main in tools.alsoAllow and the sandbox tool allowlist (group:fs is denied today; per-person memory, F041, adds `write` and `edit` only, so `read` is a grant of its own)
F041's write-path hook refusing any write under skills/, proven with a test write (needed once F041 gives the same agent a read-write workspace)
F002 photo and PDF reading with inbound attachments switched on, for the quiz's photo route only

F007 automations tool on

-main, only for the optional re-quiz reminder
F003 voice over iMessage, its local spoken replies, only for reading spelling words aloud
caveats: Asking Happy to save a skill from iMessage does not work on this stack: sandboxed runs do not construct the `skill_workshop` tool, and the documented exception would publish with no pending draft and so skip Tony's review, which is one more reason to keep that tool off every family agent.
A skill is know-how: it cannot add tools or accounts, so 'learn to order the groceries' still ends at a list.

A skill is instruction text loaded into future sessions, so one written from a pasted web page or an email is a stored injection: author only from the parent's own words, and install no marketplace skills (an audit reported by The Hacker News found 341 malicious entries among 2,857 ClawHub skills in early 2026).

Turnaround is 'when Tony next deploys', and Happy does not run a skill every time: the prompt lists only each skill's name and one-line description, so that line has to be precise, and calling the skill by name (`/skill <name>`) is the sure route where that command is accepted from the sender.

The quiz is parent-run only: the kids are not users, the parent holds the phone and sends the answers, and a version a child uses alone waits for the kids agent (F072) and never uses a cloud model or cloud speech.

The ChatGPT or Gemini app on a parent's phone already makes a quiz from uploaded material, with hints and an end summary; Happy's only edge is that it lives in the same thread and can schedule the re-quiz.
Models write wrong answer keys, especially for arithmetic and for facts the sheet does not state, so tell it to quiz only from what is on the page and spot-check.

A text quiz shows spelling words on screen, so spelling practice needs the words read aloud with the local voice (F003), whose quality for spelling words is untried, and the running score lives in the conversation and is gone after the daily session reset.

Once per-person memory (F041) gives a parent's agent `write` and `edit` on a read-write workspace, the workspace skills folder sits inside what the agent can write: for that mode the docs describe a read-only copy only for bundled, managed and plugin skills (workspace-access.md:91) and do not say the workspace skills folder is protected. 'No model-written file reaches a skills folder' then rests on F041's in-house path hook, so that hook's proof must include a refused write to skills/.
safety: Operator review is the gate: `skill_workshop` stays denied on every family agent, a skill cannot widen tool policy, and no model-written file is meant to reach a skills folder. Once per-person memory (F041) lets the same agent write files in its workspace, that last point rests on F041's write-path hook and has to be proven with a refused write to skills/. The quiz is the riskier part: a photographed school worksheet is untrusted content, is not screened by the PDF privacy gate in F002, and goes to the cloud vision model under store:false. No child's account talks to a cloud model.
unverified: Whether a user-invocable skill command typed by an allowlisted non-owner iMessage sender is accepted on 2026.9.7.
That skill sync into the sandbox works with `workspaceAccess: "none"` (the docs say sandboxed runs read materialized copies).

That a `read`-only grant on a sandboxed

-main reaches the mirrored skills and nothing private; check at build time.
Whether an iMessage owner turn is ever given library-authoring authority on this configuration. If it is, an allowlisted `skill_workshop` could publish a skill with no review.
Whether a spoken reply arrives as a playable voice message or as a file in iMessage Basic mode.
The quality of the macOS say voice for spelling words was not tried.

name: Per-person read-only mail agent: 'did I get an email about X?' on request, and a 07:00 digest of mail that needs action
description: One locked-down mail agent per adult reads that adult's own Gmail under a read-only grant: a parent asks 'did the dentist confirm?' and gets the sender, the date and the gist, and at 07:00 the same agent texts about ten lines on mail that needs a reply, has a deadline or involves money (from January to April a Saturday text adds which expected tax forms have had an arrival email). Nothing in Gmail is changed, labelled, drafted or sent, and the agent cannot browse, run code or message anyone but its owner.
example: Tony texts: 'Did the dentist confirm Thursday?' and gets the sender, the date and one line of gist from his own inbox. Trigger, 07:00, text to Tony: 'Mail that needs you: the plumber asks you to confirm Thursday's visit by tomorrow; the car insurance renewal is due on 20 October. Nothing else needs a reply.'
how:
Agent (G015): one `

-mail` entry per adult with `profile: "minimal"`, an explicit `

-gmail__*` allow plus the `tools.sandbox.tools` gate, web, fs, runtime and browser denied, memory search off; checked with `openclaw sandbox explain --agent`. Tool (F047): `gog mcp` as a host-side stdio entry under `mcp.servers`, narrowed with `--allow-tool` to the Gmail read tools (its default also registers Drive, Docs, Sheets and Calendar reads); one token per adult from `gog auth add` with `--services` limited to Gmail and `--gmail-scope readonly`. Lookup: `

-main` spawns `

-mail` through `subagents.allowAgents`. Digest (F016): an isolated 07:00 job on `

-mail` with `--tools "

-gmail__*,llm-task"`, announced to the owner only; health senders by subject line only. Tax forms (F061): a Saturday job, January to April, on the same agent.
caveats: The roadmap's M4 keeps each inbox on a local model and none is installed, so the lookup and the digest both send personal mail to the cloud model, and without Zero Data Retention the 30-day abuse-monitoring log applies to that text; this is Tony's open decision and the whole card waits on it.

Google already does much of this where the mail lives: the Gemini app answers questions from a person's own Gmail and lists a daily digest of calendar, to-dos and emails among its scheduled actions, and Gmail's 'AI Inbox' was announced in January 2026, so try those on one parent's account before building; Happy adds only asking, and being told, in the iMessage thread.
gog is not installed on this Mac, so its flags come from upstream docs and must be confirmed with `gog mcp --list-tools` and `gog auth add --help` on the installed version.
With sandbox mode all, MCP tools stay hidden unless `tools.sandbox.tools` names `bundle-mcp` or the server glob, and the minimal profile does not allow MCP tools implicitly.

A Google sign-in app left in Testing issues tokens that expire after seven days, so the app is published to In production (the consent screen then shows a warning) or each adult signs in again every week; whether both adults' tokens can share one keyring under the happy user is still open.

'Send pinned to owner' applies only when the mail agent runs its own scheduled turn, because a mail agent spawned from `

-main` always loses `message` and `session_status`; that a before_tool_call hook reaches MCP tool calls is implied by the docs but not stated.
'Memory off' is not one switch: memory search has a per-agent override, dreaming is plugin-wide, and the session-exclusion setting only matches hook sessions.

Reply drafts are left out, 'subject line only for health senders' and 'do not open the form' are instructions to the agent and not enforced limits, and the tax-form check only knows that a notice email arrived, so a form that came by post or sits in a portal shows as missing.

The lookup goes one step beyond the roadmap's design, where a mail agent's only output is its scheduled text to the owner: here the answer comes back into the parent's own agent, which holds that parent's notes and may hand a task to the research helper (F019). OpenClaw's guidance is to deny `sessions_spawn` to an agent that handles untrusted content (tool-permissions.md:21), and the roadmap already names that hand-off as its one remaining leak path, so the lookup needs its own test with a seeded misleading mail, or the card can start with the digest alone.
corrections: The 9 Oct needs list omits the sandbox-layer gate: with sandbox mode 'all', MCP tools stay hidden unless `tools.sandbox.tools` names `bundle-mcp` or the server glob (docs/gateway/config-tools/tool-policy.md:101 and :130). The minimal profile does not allow MCP tools implicitly either (same file, lines 36 and 41).

'Memory off' is not one switch in the installed docs: memory search has a per-agent override (`agents.entries.*.memory.search`, `enabled`, docs/reference/memory-config.md:31 and :102), dreaming is plugin-wide (docs/concepts/memory.md:275), and `excludeSessions.hookExternalContentSources` only matches hook sessions (docs/reference/memory-config.md:667).

'Send pinned to owner' only applies when the mail agent runs its own scheduled or hook turn: when spawned from `

-main` it always loses `message` and `session_status` (docs/tools/subagents/tool-policy.md:23), so its allow list must not consist of `session_status` alone.
The 9 Oct needs list puts `openclaw models status --agent --probe` in the deploy checks; the installed doc says a direct probe needs the Gateway stopped (docs/cli/models.md:121).

The 9 Oct verifier note says gogcli has no read-only-only Gmail scope. The upstream command reference lists `--gmail-scope full|readonly|send|read-send` and says `--readonly` on `gog auth add` requests read-only OAuth scopes, so a read-only grant can be requested; the catalog's hedge 'if the installed version supports it' can be firmed up, pending a check on the installed binary.

The 9 Oct text treats the `

-gmail` wrapper as new code. Upstream gogcli ships a stdio MCP server (`gog mcp`) that exposes only read tools unless `--allow-write` is passed, so the config entry can run gog directly with an `--allow-tool` list and no wrapper.

The 9 Oct needs list stops at the per-agent allow list. With sandbox mode 'all' (Happy's setting) the installed docs add a second gate: MCP tools are filtered out unless `tools.sandbox.tools` also names `bundle-mcp` or the server glob (docs/gateway/config-tools/tool-policy.md:101 and :130).
unverified: The per-person provider setting that sends store false was verified in M1 and not re-read here.
Whether this OpenAI account has zero retention; without it the 30-day abuse-monitoring log applies to mail text sent to the model.
Whether personal mail may go to the cloud model under store:false is Tony's open decision; no source settles it.
The promptfoo boundary and injection canaries are in-house tests, not OpenClaw features.
A before_tool_call hook reaching MCP tool calls is implied by the doc ('every tool call in the run', docs/plugins/hooks/tool-policy.md:222), but no sentence naming MCP tools was found.

gog is not installed on this Mac; its flags (`--gmail-scope readonly` and `--services` on `gog auth add`, `--allow-tool` on `gog mcp`) come from the upstream main-branch docs and must be confirmed with `gog mcp --list-tools` and `gog auth add --help` on the version Homebrew installs.

Whether both adults' tokens would sit in one keyring under the happy user: upstream says tokens use the platform keyring by default with a file backend for headless hosts; splitting them with a per-adult GOG_HOME is an inference from the paths doc.

That publishing the self-made Google sign-in app to In production, as gog's quickstart describes, keeps a read-only Gmail token alive past seven days on a personal, unverified app was not tested; Google's scope page marks gmail.readonly as a Restricted scope.

Whether Gmail's AI Inbox is available on the parents' accounts in October 2026: Google's January 2026 announcement was read, and later press coverage tying it to paid Google AI plans was seen only in search results.
safety: The mail agent holds private mail and reads untrusted mail text, so it gets no way out of its own: no web, file, code or browser tools, no draft or send tool, and texts only to the mailbox's owner. The digest runs unattended on that same agent. The lookup is the weaker half: its answer returns into the parent's own agent, which holds that parent's memory and can hand a task to the research helper, so a mail written to mislead could reach the hand-off that the roadmap names as its one remaining leak path. The relayed answer has to be treated as untrusted (a prompt rule, not an enforced limit), and a seeded-mail test has to show that it cannot make the parent's agent pass anything to research. The other open question is the model: personal mail would go to the cloud model.

name: Email me this: long answers, tables and plans sent to the asker's own inbox (owner-only mailout)
description: 'Email me this': long answers, tables and plans land in the asker's own inbox from a dedicated family sender. A hook that fails closed is meant to block any send that is not addressed to the asker alone; that block has to be proven with a test send before go-live.
example: Jordan texts: 'Email me the camp comparison.' The full table arrives in her own inbox from the family sender address. A send with anyone else on the To, cc or bcc line is meant to be blocked by the hook, and that block is tested before go-live.
how:
A send-only mail tool on a dedicated family sender account: the gog MCP server with the write flag plus its separate `--allow-gmail-send` flag and only the send tool allowed, granted to `

-main` only. A `before_tool_call` hook blocks the call unless the recipient equals the owner address of the calling agent and cc and bcc are empty; a block is terminal and the hook fails closed. Do not rely on rewriting the recipient: the docs describe rewrites for host-owned tool parameters only. An in-house daily send cap. Sign the sender account in with a send-only grant if the installed gog supports it (the upstream command reference lists a `send` mode for `--gmail-scope` on `gog auth add`), so that the token cannot read that mailbox.
caveats: The promise that nobody else can be a recipient rests on an in-house hook, and it is not yet shown that the hook sees every recipient field (to, cc, bcc) of the send tool: a seeded send to a non-owner address must be blocked before this goes live.
The hook blocks a wrong recipient; it does not correct it, because the docs describe rewriting parameters for host-owned tools only.
It needs a dedicated family sender Google account with a send grant, set up by hand outside OpenClaw, and a daily send cap that is in-house code (no built-in cap was found).
gog's quickstart says a Google sign-in app left in Testing issues tokens that expire after seven days, so the sender account needs the app published to In production, as the mail reader (G015) does.
unverified: That the hook sees every recipient field (to, cc, bcc) of the gog MCP send tool in its parameters; prove it with a seeded send to a non-owner address, which must be blocked.
A daily send cap is in-house code; no built-in cap was found in the pages read.
Creating the dedicated family sender account and granting its send scope is a manual step outside OpenClaw.

That `gog auth add --gmail-scope send` exists on the installed version and that the MCP send tool works under a send-only grant: the flag was read in the upstream command reference, and gog is not installed on this Mac.
safety: The send tool sits on each parent's own agent, which holds private data, so the recipient pin is the protection: a fail-closed hook blocks any send that is not addressed to the calling agent's owner alone, with no cc or bcc, and the tool is granted to no shared or mail-reading agent. Mail leaves from a dedicated family sender address, not from a parent's own account.
